Closed forms for the constants in the odd-weight identities
between dihedral modular graph functions
Noah Schittenhelm
Hack-Nation 2026, Team Ninja Turtles
Preprint, October 2026

Abstract We study the combinations Xw of dihedral
two-loop modular graph functions C(a, b, c) of odd
weight w whose Laplacian is proportional to the Eisenstein series Ew . We establish Xw = fw Ew +gw ζ(w) with
fw = 3 ((w − 1)/2)!/w and gw = 6|Bw−1 |/((w − 1)/2)!
at the odd weights 3 ≤ w ≤ 61. The argument combines
exact rational Laplace algebra with the Laurent constant
term evaluated in rational arithmetic from a published
theorem. That theorem and the standard lemma on
harmonic invariant functions of polynomial growth are
assumed and not machine-checked. The harmonic space
is exactly one-dimensional for odd w and zero for even
w at the weights 3 ≤ w ≤ 25. Independently of the
proof, the identities at w = 3, . . . , 17 were confirmed
numerically at 32 digits at verifier-chosen points; w = 15
was a prediction and w = 17 a preregistered blind test.
The full weight-11 basis has exactly one relation. A
hardening run exposed and fixed an evaluator bug. A
proof beyond the weights examined remains open and
is stated as a conjecture.

undetermined integration constants. Do the constants
have closed forms, and can these be established?
Why it is hard. The constant of integration requires
the Laurent polynomial of each C(a, b, c), and both the
number of graphs and the size of the coefficients grow
with w. Numerical determination by integer-relation
searches is limited by working precision relative to coefficient height. An exact route is available through the
Laurent polynomial of the two-loop modular graph functions (Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:1902.04180). That theorem
was not evaluated for these identities there.
Contribution. We evaluate it in rational arithmetic
and obtain closed forms for fw and gw at the odd weights
3 ≤ w ≤ 61 examined. We also give an exact uniqueness
statement and independent numerical confirmations.
Summary of results.
• Theorem 1 shows Xw = fw Ew + gw ζ(w) with fw =
3((w − 1)/2)!/w and gw = 6|Bw−1 |/((w − 1)/2)! at
the odd weights 3 ≤ w ≤ 61 (exact; proof in three
steps with two stated assumptions).
• Theorem 2 shows that the space {X : ∆X ∈ QEw }
is one-dimensional for odd w and zero for even w
at the weights 3 ≤ w ≤ 25 (exact).
• Conjecture 1 states the closed forms beyond the
examined range; they are established only for 3 ≤
w ≤ 61.
• The numerical observations confirm the identities
independently of the proof at w = 3, . . . , 17. The
full weight-11 basis has exactly one relation, and a
hardening run is reported.

1 Introduction
Dihedral modular graph functions C(a, b, c) arise as
coefficients in the low-energy expansion of the oneloop closed-string amplitude. D’Hoker, Green and Vanhove showed that they satisfy Laplace eigenvalue equations with inhomogeneous terms polynomial in nonholomorphic Eisenstein series, and they exhibited exact
differential and algebraic relations for an infinite class of
such functions [1]. The Laplace equation fixes an algebraic relation only up to an additive constant of integration, which is obtained from the asymptotics at the cusp
[1]. In the simplest cases this gives C(1, 1, 1) = E3 +ζ(3)
and C(2, 2, 1) = 25 E5 +ζ(5)/30. At weight 7 the identity
C(3, 3, 1) + C(3, 2, 2) = 37 E7 + ζ(7)/252 appears in a
later hierarchy of modular graph identities [2]. Related
relations between graphs with four and five links, and
between higher-loop graphs, were also treated in the
literature [3, 4].
